g1.title: Lesson 1: Counting & Number Identification 1. (1-10)
g1.lecture: Hello, young wizard! Today we will learn to count from 1 to 10.

lecture_steps.text: Hello, young wizard! Every magic spell starts with counting. Today we will count from 1 to 10 together!
Are you ready to count with me?
Great! Look at the numbers. When a number lights up, say it out loud with me. Ready?
Well done! You counted from 1 to 10. Your magic is getting stronger!
Now it is your turn. Tap one golden acorn at a time. Say the next number each time you tap.
This one is a little tricky! Count only the glowing stars. Skip the empty boxes. Can you find every star?
Here is a wizard secret: when you count, the last number you say tells you how many there are!
You did great, wizard! Now let's play the trial. Take your time. I believe in you!

questions.text: Count the golden acorns. Start on the left and go to the right. How many are there?
Put these floating numbers in counting order, from smallest to biggest: 2, 5, 4, 8.
Some boxes have a glowing orb and some boxes are empty. Count only the boxes with an orb. How many are there?
Put the numbers 9, 3, 7 and 1 in order, from biggest to smallest.
Arith has 7 magic books. He counts them, starting from 1. What is the last number he says?
Matthew sees glowing numbers in the trees: 3, 4, 5. What number comes next?
Count the flowers in the garden one by one. How many flowers are there in all?
Count Matthew's shards one by one. How many shards does Matthew have?
Mr. Minus has 5 spell scrolls. He counts backward, starting at 5. What is the last number he says?
Matthew counts his 5 pencils. What number comes after 5?

g1.title: Lesson 2: Comparing Numbers
g1.lecture: A magic balance shows which side has more. The heavier side goes down. If both sides have the same amount, it stays flat.

lecture_steps.text: Meet the magic balance! It always tells us which side has more.
Look! The right side has more runes, so that side goes down. The heavier side always goes down.
Remember: the side with the bigger number goes down.
Now both sides have the same amount, so the balance stays flat. We call this equal!
7 is greater than 4. Greater means bigger!
And 4 is less than 7. Less means smaller!
Your turn, young wizard! Look at the balance. Which side goes down?
Amazing! You can compare numbers like a real wizard!

questions.text: Mr. Archimedes puts 4 glowing runes on the left side of the balance and 6 glowing runes on the right side. Which side has more?
Matthew puts his golden acorns on the left side of the balance. Arith puts his on the right side. Look at the balance. Which side is heavier?
questions.hint: The heavier side goes down lower. Which side is going down?
questions.explanation: The left side has 5 acorns. The right side has 3 acorns. 5 is more than 3, so the left side goes down. It is heavier!

questions.text: Ms. Addria puts 6 crystal shards on one side of the balance. How many shards must she put on the other side to make both sides equal?
Your potion needs 3 mana drops, but you have only 2. Is what you have greater than or less than what the potion needs?
Baker Pip puts 5 buns on the left side of the balance and 5 pies on the right side. Look at the balance. Which symbol shows how the two numbers compare?
questions.hint: Is one side lower than the other, or are both sides flat?
questions.explanation: Both sides have 5, so the balance stays flat. No side is heavier, so they are equal!

questions.text: The heavier side of the balance goes down. One side has 5 coins and the other side has 3 coins. Which number is greater and makes the balance go down?
Which side of the balance is heavier: the left side with 5 orbs, or the right side with 3 orbs? Type the number of orbs on the heavier side.
questions.hint: Count each side. The side with more is heavier!
questions.explanation: 5 is more than 3, so the left side with 5 orbs is heavier!

questions.text: Arith puts 3 magic orbs on the left side of the balance and 6 magic orbs on the right side. Which side is heavier? Type the number of orbs on that side.
questions.hint: Count each side. The side with more is heavier!
questions.explanation: 6 is more than 3, so the right side with 6 orbs is heavier!

questions.text: The Great Math Wizard wants a number that is bigger than 7 but smaller than 9. What number is it?
Matthew puts 3 fire crystals on the left side of the balance and 4 ice crystals on the right side. Is the left side greater than, less than, or equal to the right side?

g1.title: Lesson 3: Counting & Number Identification 2. (1-20)
g1.lecture: After ten come the teen numbers: eleven, twelve, all the way to twenty. Start at ten, then count on one more each time.

lecture_steps.text: Let's count past ten and meet the teen numbers! A teen number is ten and a little bit more.
Are you ready to count from 11 to 20?
Here are 10 stars and 6 more. Start at ten, then count on: eleven, twelve... Tap each extra star!
Ten and six more make sixteen! Counting on is a fast wizard trick.
Your turn! There are 10 stars and 3 more. How many stars are there in all?
Wonderful! Now you can count to twenty!

questions.text: Matthew has 14 fire crystals. He finds one more. What number comes right after 14?
Mr. Archimedes puts all his golden acorns on his desk. Count them. How many golden acorns are there in all?
Matthew sees glowing numbers in the trees: 11, 12, 13. What are the next two numbers?
Arith has one chest with 10 magic stars and another chest with 10 magic stars. How many magic stars does he have in all?
Put these numbers in counting order, from smallest to biggest: 15, 12, 17, 14.
The Great Math Wizard asks you to count backward to open a door. You start at 20. What are the next three numbers you say?
Matthew is putting his spell scrolls in order. Which number is missing: 16, 17, _, 19, 20?
Ms. Addria puts crystal shards on both sides of the balance. Look at the balance. Which side is heavier?
questions.hint: The heavier side goes down lower. Which side is going down?
questions.explanation: The left side has 3 shards. The right side has 6 shards. 6 is more than 3, so the right side goes down. It is heavier!

questions.text: Matthew counts 15 blue lilies in the garden. What number did he say just before 15?
Put the numbers 18, 11, 20 and 16 in order, from biggest to smallest.

g1.title: Lesson 4: Comparing & Ordering Numbers
g1.lecture: Every shape has straight sides that we can count. We can compare shapes by their sides, just like numbers.

lecture_steps.text: Every shape has a secret number: its sides! Let's count them together.
Tap each glowing side and count with me. A triangle has 3 sides!
Now the square. Tap each side and count. A square has 4 sides!
The square has 4 sides. The triangle has 3 sides. 4 is more than 3, so the square has more sides!
Your turn, shape detective! Which shape has fewer sides? Fewer means less.
Brilliant! You can compare shapes like a real wizard!

questions.text: Professor Bound draws two shapes: a triangle with 3 sides and a square with 4 sides. Which shape has MORE sides?
options: both have the same number of sides
questions.explanation: Count the sides. The triangle has 3 and the square has 4. 4 is more than 3, so the square has more!

visual.instruction: Tap each side to count it, then pick the shape with more sides.

questions.text: Matthew finds a star rune with 10 sides and an ice crystal with 12 sides. Does the star rune have less than, greater than, or equal to the sides of the ice crystal?
questions.explanation: The star rune has 10 sides. The ice crystal has 12. 10 is less than 12, so the answer is less than!

visual.instruction: Compare the number of sides on each shape.

questions.text: Two magic flowers grow by the window. One is a pentagon with 5 sides. One is a triangle with 3 sides. Which flower has MORE sides?
questions.explanation: The pentagon has 5 sides and the triangle has 3. 5 is more than 3, so the pentagon has more!

visual.instruction: Tap the sides to count them!

questions.text: Arith's magic shield has 5 sides. Matthew's shield has 3 sides. Whose shield has MORE sides?
questions.explanation: Arith's shield has 5 sides and Matthew's has 3. 5 is more than 3, so Arith's shield has more sides!

visual.instruction: Tap the sides of each shield to count them!

questions.text: Put these shapes in order, from the FEWEST sides to the MOST sides: a hexagon (6 sides), a triangle (3 sides), and an octagon (8 sides).
questions.explanation: The triangle has 3, the hexagon has 6, and the octagon has 8. From fewest to most: 3, 6, 8!

visual.instruction: Put the numbers of sides in order, smallest first.

questions.text: Matthew draws a heptagon with 7 sides next to a square with 4 sides. Which sentence is true?
questions.explanation: The heptagon has 7 sides and the square has 4. 7 is more than 4, so '7 is greater than 4' is true!

visual.instruction: Tap the sides to count them!

questions.text: Ms. Addria draws a hexagon with 6 sides. Matthew wants to draw a twin shape with the same number of sides. How many sides does his shape need?
questions.explanation: A twin shape has the same number of sides. The hexagon has 6, so Matthew's shape needs 6 sides too!

visual.instruction: Tap each side of the hexagon to count it!

questions.text: The Great Math Wizard shows a shape with 11 sides and another shape with 13 sides. He wants a shape with MORE than 11 sides but FEWER than 13. How many sides must it have?
questions.explanation: The number between 11 and 13 is 12. Count on: 11, 12, 13!

questions.text: Put these treasures in order, from the MOST sides to the FEWEST sides: a 19-sided crystal, a 15-sided gem, and a 20-sided rune.
questions.explanation: The rune has 20 sides, the crystal has 19, and the gem has 15. From most to fewest: 20, 19, 15!

visual.instruction: Put the numbers of sides in order, biggest first.

questions.text: Baker Pip bakes a pie in a pentagon pan with 5 sides. Baker Dave bakes a pie in a square pan with 4 sides. Whose pan has MORE sides?
questions.explanation: Baker Pip's pan has 5 sides and Baker Dave's pan has 4. 5 is more than 4, so Baker Pip's pan has more sides!

visual.instruction: Tap the sides of each pan to count them!

g1.title: Lesson 5: Counting & Number Identification 3. (1-50)
g1.lecture: Let's count up to fifty! One more means the next number. Counting down means the number before.

lecture_steps.text: Time for a bigger adventure! Let's climb all the way up to fifty.
Are you ready to count by tens? Counting by tens is like taking giant steps!
Counting on by one: one more than 42 is 43.
And one more than 49 is 50. We reached a new ten!
Counting down goes backward, like a countdown: 10, 9, 8, 7!
Your turn! What number comes right after 47?
Hooray! You reached fifty. What a climb!

questions.text: Matthew finds a chest in the forest. He counts 42 gold coins. Then he finds one more coin. How many coins does he have now?
Mr. Archimedes wants you to fill in the blank. Which number is missing: 38, 39, __, 41, 42?
Baker Pip counts 50 pies. What number did he say just before 50?
Ms. Addria says the number 'forty-seven'. How do you write it with digits?
Matthew sees glowing numbers in the trees. Put 25, 29, 22 and 27 in counting order, from smallest to biggest.
Arith starts at 38 and counts forward three steps. What number does he reach?
The Great Math Wizard wants you to count backward from 30. What are the next three numbers you say?
Mr. Archimedes has 49 golden acorns. He finds one more. How many does he have in all?
Which side of the balance is heavier: the left side with 6 magic gems, or the right side with 4 gems? Type the number of gems on the heavier side.
questions.hint: Count each side. The side with more is heavier!
questions.explanation: 6 is more than 4, so the left side with 6 gems is heavier!

questions.text: Matthew gets 50 EXP, 15 EXP and 35 EXP. Put these amounts in order, from biggest to smallest.

g1.title: Lesson 6: Place Value - Tens & Ones
g1.lecture: We pack things into groups of ten. The groups are the tens. The extra things are the ones. Remember: one ten is 10, so 2 tens are 20.

lecture_steps.text: Wizards are tidy! We pack coins into bundles of ten. Then we can count them faster.
Tap each bundle and count by tens: ten, twenty, thirty...
You have 20 gold coins in bundles, and 5 loose coins. The loose coins are the ones. How many gold coins are there in all?
2 tens and 5 ones make 25. Say the tens first, then the ones!
Your turn! 3 tens and 4 ones make which number?
Great! You count like a royal treasurer! Now let's try the trial.

questions.text: Mr. Tenz shows you 2 chests. Each chest has 10 gold coins. There are also 5 loose coins. How many gold coins are there in all?
Which number sentence makes 42?
Look at these 3 chests. How many stars are there in all?
Arith finds 4 full chests. Each chest has 10 ice crystals. How many ice crystals does he have in all?
Matthew puts 3 gold coins on the left side of the balance and 5 gold coins on the right side. Which side is heavier? Type the number of coins on that side.
questions.hint: Count each side. The side with more is heavier!
questions.explanation: 5 is more than 3, so the right side with 5 coins is heavier!

questions.text: Baker Pip has 18 buns. He packs them in full bags of 10. How many full bags can he make?
Matthew has 4 tens and 9 ones. What number is that?
You have 2 boxes of gold coins. The first box has 24 coins. The second box has 16 coins. How many gold coins do you have in all?
You need 36 EXP to open a door. You have 30 EXP now. How many more EXP do you need?
Matthew has 2 chests of ten gold coins, 1 chest of ten crystals, and 4 loose coins. How many things does he have in all?

g1.title: Lesson 7: Counting & Number Identification 4. (1-80)
g1.lecture: Let's count up to eighty! Each number is one more than the number before it. A missing number is easy to find.

lecture_steps.text: Let's go even higher, all the way up to eighty!
Are you ready to take giant steps of ten again?
One more than 67 is 68. Just one small step!
A number is missing between 59 and 61. It is 60!
Your turn, number hunter! Find the missing number.
You reached eighty! Your counting magic is getting stronger!

questions.text: Matthew counts 67 fire crystals. He finds one more. What number comes right after 67?
Mr. Archimedes writes a pattern on the board. Which number is missing: 71, 72, __, 74, 75?
Baker Pip baked 80 star-fruit buns. What number did he say just before 80?
How do you write the number 'seventy-six' with digits?
Arith finds spell scrolls with numbers on them. Put 55, 68, 42 and 79 in order, from smallest to biggest.
Matthew starts at 77 and counts forward three steps. What is the last number he says?
The Great Math Wizard wants you to count backward. Start at 60. What are the next three numbers?
Arith fills both sides of the balance with glowing crystals. Look at the balance. Which side is heavier?
questions.hint: The heavier side goes down lower. Which side is going down?
questions.explanation: The left side has 7 crystals. The right side has 3. 7 is more than 3, so the left side goes down. It is heavier!

questions.text: Matthew sees glowing numbers in the trees. What number comes between 59 and 61?
To open the library door, put these numbers in order, from biggest to smallest: 61, 78, 54, 80.

g1.title: Lesson 8: Basic Addition & Subtraction
g1.lecture: Listen for clue words! 'Sum', 'in all' and 'total' mean we add. 'Left', 'remaining' and 'difference' mean we take away.

lecture_steps.text: Word problems hide clue words, like secret spells. Let's learn to find them!
45 crystals, and then 20 more. 'More' and 'in all' tell us to add! 45 plus 20 is 65.
78 buns, and 30 were sold. 'How many are left?' tells us to take away! 78 minus 30 is 48.
Add when you hear sum, in all, or total. Take away when you hear left or remaining.
Your turn! 30 stars and 12 more. How many stars are there in all?
Great detective work! You found the clue words!

questions.text: Matthew finds 45 fire crystals. Arith gives him 20 more. How many fire crystals does Matthew have in all?
Baker Pip baked 78 star-fruit buns. He sold 30 of them. How many buns are left?
Ms. Addria asks: what is the sum of 32 magic stars and 14 magic stars?
The Great Math Wizard has 65 spell scrolls. He puts 12 of them away in the vault. How many scrolls are remaining on the shelf?
Matthew finds 50 golden acorns near the academy and 25 more in the forest. How many golden acorns did he find in total?
Mr. Minus asks: what is the difference between 80 ice crystals and 50 ice crystals?
Arith has 60 mana drops. He uses 20 drops to make a potion. How many mana drops are left?
At the market, Matthew buys 44 honey biscuits and 22 berry rolls. How many treats did he buy in all?
A chest has 75 silver coins. Matthew takes out 40 coins to buy a book. How many coins are remaining in the chest?
Mr. Archimedes asks: what is the sum of 55 glowing runes and 24 glowing runes?

g1.title: Lesson 9: Counting & Number Identification 5. (1-100)
g1.lecture: Let's count up to one hundred! After every ten, the pattern starts again. Missing numbers are easy to find.

lecture_steps.text: This is a big one: let's count all the way to one hundred!
Are you ready to count by tens all the way to the top?
98, 99, and then a new number: 100!
Which number fills the gap between 90 and 92? It is 91!
Your turn! What number comes right after 99?
One hundred! You reached the top of the mountain!

questions.text: Matthew counts 98 fire crystals. He finds one more. What number comes right after 98?
Mr. Archimedes writes a pattern on the board. Which number is missing: 89, 90, __, 92, 93?
Baker Pip bakes 100 star-fruit buns. What number did he say just before 100?
How do you write the number 'ninety-seven' with digits?
Arith finds magic books with numbers on them. Put 84, 99, 81 and 93 in order, from smallest to biggest.
Matthew starts at 95 and counts forward four steps to the castle gate. What is the last number he says?
The Great Math Wizard wants you to count backward. Start at 90. What are the next three numbers?
Which side of the balance is heavier: the left side with 6 sparkles, or the right side with 3 sparkles? Type the number of sparkles on the heavier side.
questions.hint: Count each side. The side with more is heavier!
questions.explanation: 6 is more than 3, so the left side with 6 sparkles is heavier!

questions.text: Matthew sees glowing numbers in the trees. What number comes between 98 and 100?
To open the last door, put these numbers in order, from biggest to smallest: 91, 100, 88, 97.

g1.title: Lesson 10: The Great Math Wizard's Final Trial
g1.lecture: The Final Trial! Use counting, comparing, tens and ones, adding and taking away to solve every puzzle.

lecture_steps.text: This is the Great Math Wizard's Final Trial! Use everything you learned. You can do it!
Are you ready for the trial, brave wizard?
First, counting on: 98, 99, 100!
Ten chests with ten coins each make 100 coins. Tens are powerful!
We spend 50 coins and then 40 coins. First we add them: 50 plus 40 is 90.
We had 100 coins and spent 90. So 10 coins are left. We take away!
You are a Grand Math Champion! I am so proud of you!

questions.text: The Great Math Wizard fills the sky with stars. You count them and reach 98. What are the last two numbers you say to reach 100?
The Wizard puts 100 mana crystals on the left side of the balance and 99 on the right side. Which symbol makes this true: >, <, or =?
The Wizard shows 10 magic chests. Each chest holds 10 gold coins. How many gold coins are there in all?
Matthew starts with 80 EXP. The Wizard gives him 10 more EXP for being brave, and 10 more EXP for being wise. What is the sum of his EXP?
Fill in the missing numbers on the castle steps: 95, 96, __, 98, __, 100.
The Wizard's library has 100 spell scrolls. He puts 20 of them in the vault. How many scrolls are remaining?
Put these power levels in order, from biggest to smallest: 88, 100, 79, 93.
The Wizard makes a number with 9 tens and 9 ones. What is the number, and how much more do you need to reach 100?
Arith puts his golden acorns on the left side of the balance. Matthew puts his on the right side. Look at the balance. Which side is heavier?
questions.hint: The heavier side goes down lower. Which side is going down?
questions.explanation: Arith's side has 5 acorns. Matthew's side has 7. 7 is more than 5, so the right side goes down. It is heavier!

questions.text: Matthew wants a book for 50 gold coins and some mana pies for 40 coins. He pays with a 100-coin pouch. How much change does he get back?

g2.title: Lesson 1: 2-Digit Addition (No Regrouping)
g2.lecture: To add big numbers, add the ones first. Then add the tens. Then put the two answers together.

lecture_steps.text: Welcome to Grade 2, young wizard! Adding big numbers is easy. First add the ones, then add the tens.
Apprentice Pip has 61 pouches. He finds 15 more. Let's add them, step by step!
First, the ones. 1 + 5 makes 6 ones.
Next, the tens. 6 tens + 1 ten makes 7 tens.
Now put them together: 7 tens and 6 ones make 76!
Your turn! What is 34 + 25?
Excellent! You can add tens and ones like a pro!

questions.text: Apprentice Pip found 61 star dust pouches in the morning. He found 15 more in the afternoon. How many did he find in all?
Apprentice Pip found 24 magic feathers in the morning. He found 14 more in the afternoon. How many did he find in all?
Apprentice Pip found 53 dragon scales in the morning. He found 15 more in the afternoon. How many did he find in all?
Apprentice Pip found 31 star dust pouches in the morning. He found 34 more in the afternoon. How many did he find in all?
Apprentice Pip found 74 magic feathers in the morning. He found 24 more in the afternoon. How many did he find in all?
Apprentice Pip found 42 magic feathers in the morning. He found 21 more in the afternoon. How many did he find in all?
Apprentice Pip found 21 magic feathers in the morning. He found 65 more in the afternoon. How many did he find in all?
Apprentice Pip found 64 dragon scales in the morning. He found 15 more in the afternoon. How many did he find in all?
Apprentice Pip found 32 dragon scales in the morning. He found 41 more in the afternoon. How many did he find in all?
Apprentice Pip found 12 dragon scales in the morning. He found 81 more in the afternoon. How many did he find in all?

g2.title: Lesson 2: 2-Digit Addition (With Regrouping)
g2.lecture: When the ones add up to ten or more, we regroup. Ten ones make one new ten. We carry that ten over to the tens.

lecture_steps.text: Sometimes the ones add up to ten or more. Then we regroup: ten ones become one new ten!
56 pixies are here, and 14 more fly in. Let's add them!
First, the ones: 6 ones + 4 ones makes 10 ones. Ten ones become one new ten!
Now the tens: 5 tens + 1 ten, plus the 1 ten we carried, makes 7 tens.
7 tens and 0 ones make 70!
Your turn! What is 38 + 27?
You did it! Regrouping is a powerful spell!

questions.text: The forest has 56 pixies on the north side and 14 pixies on the south side. How many pixies are there in all?
The forest has 48 goblins on the north side and 22 goblins on the south side. How many goblins are there in all?
The forest has 29 goblins on the north side and 55 goblins on the south side. How many goblins are there in all?
The forest has 19 fire salamanders on the north side and 34 fire salamanders on the south side. How many fire salamanders are there in all?
The forest has 66 pixies on the north side and 15 pixies on the south side. How many pixies are there in all?
The forest has 35 goblins on the north side and 35 goblins on the south side. How many goblins are there in all?
The forest has 68 pixies on the north side and 12 pixies on the south side. How many pixies are there in all?
The forest has 48 crystal frogs on the north side and 17 crystal frogs on the south side. How many crystal frogs are there in all?
The forest has 36 goblins on the north side and 19 goblins on the south side. How many goblins are there in all?
The forest has 46 goblins on the north side and 47 goblins on the south side. How many goblins are there in all?

g2.title: Lesson 3: 2-Digit Subtraction (No Regrouping)
g2.lecture: To take away big numbers, take away the ones first. Then take away the tens. Then put the two answers together.

lecture_steps.text: Taking away is magic too! First take away the ones, then take away the tens.
Wizard Alaric has 54 scrolls. He gives away 21 of them.
First, the ones: 4 - 1 is 3 ones.
Next, the tens: 5 tens - 2 tens is 3 tens.
Put them together: 3 tens and 3 ones. 33 scrolls are left!
Your turn! What is 78 - 35?
Wonderful! You can take away like a pro!

questions.text: Wizard Alaric had 54 spell scrolls. He gave 21 of them to his students. How many spell scrolls does he have left?
Wizard Alaric had 79 healing potions. He gave 46 of them to his students. How many healing potions does he have left?
Wizard Alaric had 77 spell scrolls. He gave 24 of them to his students. How many spell scrolls does he have left?
Wizard Alaric had 99 enchanted berries. He gave 56 of them to his students. How many enchanted berries does he have left?
Wizard Alaric had 54 silver coins. He gave 42 of them to his students. How many silver coins does he have left?
Wizard Alaric had 54 spell scrolls. He gave 13 of them to his students. How many spell scrolls does he have left?
Wizard Alaric had 86 silver coins. He gave 31 of them to his students. How many silver coins does he have left?
Wizard Alaric had 74 silver coins. He gave 61 of them to his students. How many silver coins does he have left?
Wizard Alaric had 86 silver coins. He gave 72 of them to his students. How many silver coins does he have left?
Wizard Alaric had 69 healing potions. He gave 28 of them to his students. How many healing potions does he have left?

g2.title: Lesson 4: 2-Digit Subtraction (With Regrouping)
g2.lecture: If the top ones number is too small, borrow one ten. That ten becomes ten ones. Add them to the ones, then take away.

lecture_steps.text: What if the top ones are too small to take away from? We borrow a ten! Watch closely.
73 potions, and 44 are sold. Oh no: 3 is smaller than 4! We cannot take it away yet.
So we borrow one ten from the tens. Now 3 becomes 13, and 13 - 4 is 9 ones.
We borrowed one ten, so the 7 tens became 6 tens. 6 tens - 4 tens is 2 tens.
2 tens and 9 ones make 29!
Your turn! What is 52 - 27?
You did it! Borrowing is a tricky spell, and you learned it!

questions.text: The potion master made 73 strength draughts. The knights bought 44 of them. How many strength draughts are left in the shop?
The potion master made 82 strength draughts. The knights bought 36 of them. How many strength draughts are left in the shop?
The potion master made 84 levitation elixirs. The knights bought 36 of them. How many levitation elixirs are left in the shop?
The potion master made 92 levitation elixirs. The knights bought 36 of them. How many levitation elixirs are left in the shop?
The potion master made 54 strength draughts. The knights bought 29 of them. How many strength draughts are left in the shop?
The potion master made 44 invisibility potions. The knights bought 18 of them. How many invisibility potions are left in the shop?
The potion master made 71 strength draughts. The knights bought 43 of them. How many strength draughts are left in the shop?
The potion master made 44 truth serums. The knights bought 19 of them. How many truth serums are left in the shop?
The potion master made 54 levitation elixirs. The knights bought 17 of them. How many levitation elixirs are left in the shop?
The potion master made 93 strength draughts. The knights bought 49 of them. How many strength draughts are left in the shop?

g2.title: Lesson 5: Intro to Multiplication (Arrays)
g2.lecture: An array has equal rows. Count by the number in each row, one time for each row. Multiplying means adding equal groups.

lecture_steps.text: An array is a magic grid with neat, equal rows. It helps us count really fast!
Here are 4 rows of 4. Tap each row and count by fours: 4, 8, 12, 16!
4 rows of 4 make 16. We write it as 4 x 4!
Now there are 5 rows of 3. Tap each row and count by threes: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15!
5 rows of 3 make 15. We write it as 5 x 3!
Your turn! 3 rows of 4. How many are there in all?
Arrays are easy for you! Great job!

questions.text: In the armory, the crystal balls stand in 4 rows. Each row has 4 crystal balls. How many crystal balls are there in all?
In the armory, the spell books stand in 5 rows. Each row has 3 spell books. How many spell books are there in all?
In the armory, the spell books stand in 5 rows. Each row has 5 spell books. How many spell books are there in all?
In the armory, the crystal balls stand in 2 rows. Each row has 5 crystal balls. How many crystal balls are there in all?
In the armory, the flying brooms stand in 3 rows. Each row has 5 flying brooms. How many flying brooms are there in all?
In the armory, the magic wands stand in 5 rows. Each row has 5 magic wands. How many magic wands are there in all?
In the armory, the magic wands stand in 3 rows. Each row has 2 magic wands. How many magic wands are there in all?
In the armory, the crystal balls stand in 5 rows. Each row has 4 crystal balls. How many crystal balls are there in all?
In the armory, the crystal balls stand in 2 rows. Each row has 5 crystal balls. How many crystal balls are there in all?

g2.title: Lesson 6: Fraction Words to Numbers
g2.lecture: A fraction is a whole cut into equal pieces. The bottom number tells how many pieces there are in all. The top number tells how many pieces we take.

lecture_steps.text: A fraction is a whole cut into equal pieces, like slices of a magic pie!
The pie has 2 equal pieces, and we take 1. That is one half!
Now there are 3 equal pieces, and we take 2. That is two thirds!
Now there are 4 equal pieces, and we take 3. That is three fourths!
The top number tells how many pieces we take. The bottom number tells how many pieces there are in all.
Your turn! How much of the shape is colored? Write it as a fraction.
Fractions unlocked! You are slicing up the magic!

g2.title: Lesson 7: Counting the Sides of Shapes
g2.lecture: A side is a straight edge. Go around the shape and count each side one time. If there are more shapes, add all their sides.

lecture_steps.text: A side is a straight edge of a shape. Let's be shape detectives and count them!
Tap each side and count with me: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5!
Look at all these shapes: 3, 4, 5, 6, and 8 sides. Each one is different!
A square and a triangle together: 4 + 3 makes 7 sides.

g2.title: Lesson 8: Time (To the 5 Minutes)
g2.lecture: The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes. Count by fives: each number on the clock is five more minutes.

lecture_steps.text: A clock has two magic hands. Let's learn how to read them!
The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes.
The long hand points to 4. Count by fives four times: that is 20 minutes. So it is 12:20!
The long hand points to 1. That is just 5 minutes. So it is 12:05!
Your turn! What time does this clock show?
You are a time master! The clock tower is proud of you!

g2.title: Lesson 9: Mixed Addition & Subtraction
g2.lecture: Work from left to right, one step at a time. 'Finds' and 'more' mean add. 'Gives away' and 'uses' mean take away.

lecture_steps.text: Some puzzles have two steps. Work from left to right, one step at a time!
Pip has 45 and finds 23 more. Finding means we add: 45 + 23 is 68.
Then Pip gives away 18. Giving away means we take away: 68 - 18 leaves 50!
Add when someone finds, gets, or receives more. Take away when someone gives away or uses some.
Your turn! What is 20 + 15 - 8?
Two steps, no problem! You are unstoppable!

g2.title: Lesson 10: Mixed Addition & Subtraction with Parentheses
g2.lecture: Parentheses ( ) are a signal: solve this part first! Then finish the rest, from left to right.

lecture_steps.text: Parentheses are like a magic shield. They mean: solve this part first!
A wizard has 50 coins. He buys a wand and a hat. First, solve 12 + 8 inside the parentheses.
Inside the parentheses: 12 + 8 makes 20.
Then take away: 50 - 20 leaves 30 coins!
Your turn! Remember: parentheses first. What is the answer?
Parentheses first, every time! Brilliant!

g3.title: Lesson 1: Multiplication Tables (1-10)
g3.lecture: Multiplying is a fast way to add equal groups. Dividing shares things fairly. 'Each' and 'product' mean multiply. 'Split equally' means divide.

lecture_steps.text: Welcome to Grade 3! Multiplying is a fast way to add equal groups.
Here are 5 groups, and each group has 5 coins. Together they make 25 coins.
5 x 5 = 25. The answer to a multiplication is called the product!
Dividing means fair sharing. Share 40 among 8 friends, and each friend gets 5. The answer to a division is called the quotient!
Clue words: 'each' and 'product' mean multiply. 'Split equally' means divide.
Your turn! What is 6 x 4?
You know your times tables! You are a multiplying marvel!

g3.title: Lesson 2: Multiplication Word Problems
g3.lecture: Look for clue words! 'Each' means equal groups, so we multiply. The product is the answer to a multiplication.

lecture_steps.text: Word problems hide clues. Look for words like 'each' and 'product'!
Matthew buys 4 packs. Each pack has 5 cards.
Every pack has the same number of cards, so we multiply: 4 x 5 = 20 cards!
The product of 6 and 3 is 18. Product means multiply!
Your turn! 5 bags, and each bag has 3 gems. How many gems are there in all?
Clue hunter! You cracked the code!

g3.title: Lesson 3: Division Concepts (Equal Sharing)
g3.lecture: Division means sharing a total equally. It is like multiplication, but backward.

lecture_steps.text: Division means sharing things equally, so everyone gets a fair share.
20 gems are shared by 4 wizards. Each wizard gets 5!
We write it like this: 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
We can check with multiplication: 4 x 5 = 20. It matches!
Your turn! What is 15 ÷ 3?
Fair sharing! Every wizard is happy!

g3.title: Lesson 4: Division Word Problems
g3.lecture: The answer to a division is called the quotient. Share the total equally, then find how many each one gets.

lecture_steps.text: The answer to a division is called the quotient. Let's find some!
27 magic sparks go into 3 jars, the same number in each jar. Each jar gets 9!
27 ÷ 3 = 9. So the quotient is 9.
42 rings are shared by 6 friends. Each friend gets 7. The quotient is 7!
Your turn! What is 35 ÷ 5?
Quotient found! You are a division detective!

g3.title: Lesson 5: Equivalent & Comparing Fractions
g3.lecture: If the bottom numbers are the same, compare the top numbers. Equivalent fractions look different, but they are the same amount.

lecture_steps.text: When the fraction pieces are the same size, we just compare the top numbers!
3 pieces is more than 1 piece.
So 3/4 is bigger than 1/4!
Look closely: 1/2 and 2/4 cover the very same amount.
Same amount, but different numbers. We call them equivalent!
Your turn! Which fraction is the same amount as 1/2?
Fraction expert! That was clever thinking!

g3.title: Lesson 6: Basic MDAS
g3.lecture: MDAS tells us the order: first multiply and divide, then add and subtract. Always go from left to right.

lecture_steps.text: In a spell, the order matters! Always multiply and divide before you add and subtract.
In 5 + 3 x 4, we multiply first: 3 x 4 = 12.
Then we add: 5 + 12 = 17. It is not 32!
In 18 ÷ 3 + 7, we divide first: 18 ÷ 3 = 6.
Then we add: 6 + 7 = 13!
Your turn! What is 2 + 6 x 3? Remember the order!
MDAS mastered! Your spells are in perfect order!

g3.title: Lesson 7: Basic PMDAS
g3.lecture: PMDAS tells us the order: first parentheses, then multiply and divide, then add and subtract.

lecture_steps.text: Parentheses are the first step of the spell. Always solve inside them first!
In (5 + 3) x 4, we solve inside the parentheses first.
In 20 ÷ (2 + 3), we solve inside first: 2 + 3 = 5.
Your turn! What is (6 + 4) x 2?
PMDAS mastered! Your magic follows every rule!

g3.title: Lesson 8: Elapsed Time
g3.lecture: Elapsed time is how much time passes. To find the end time, add the time to the start. To find how long, count from the start to the end.

lecture_steps.text: Elapsed time means how much time passes. Let's see how long our potions take!
A potion starts cooking at 2:00. It takes 45 minutes.
Add 45 minutes to 2:00. The potion is ready at 2:45!
Magic class starts at 9:00 and ends at 10:20. How long is that?
From 9:00 to 10:00 is 1 hour. Then 20 more minutes. So it is 1 hour and 20 minutes!
Your turn! A spell starts at 3:00 and lasts 30 minutes. When does it end?
Time traveler! You tamed the clock!

g3.title: Lesson 9: Volume & Mass
g3.lecture: Volume is how much space a liquid fills. Mass is how heavy something is. 1 kilogram is the same as 1,000 grams.

lecture_steps.text: Potion makers measure everything! Volume is how much space a liquid fills. Mass is how heavy something is.
15 liters + 5 liters makes 20 liters of magic water.
Remember this secret: 1 kilogram is the same as 1,000 grams!
450 grams + 300 grams makes 750 grams.
Your turn! Which one is heavier?
Measuring ace! Your measurements are perfect!

g3.title: Lesson 10: Advanced PMDAS
g3.lecture: Go one careful step at a time: parentheses, then multiply and divide, then add and subtract. Work from the inside out.

lecture_steps.text: This is the most powerful spell yet! Go one careful step at a time: Parentheses, then Multiply and Divide, then Add and Subtract.
First, the parentheses: 3 + 4 = 7.
Next, multiply and divide: 2 x 7 = 14, and 18 ÷ 6 = 3.
Last, add: 14 + 3 = 17!
Parentheses inside parentheses? Start with the one in the middle, then work your way out.
In the end, 20 ÷ 5 = 4!
Your turn! What is (4 + 2) x 3?
Diamond Medal! You learned the most powerful math spell!
